subject: physical-education
title: Investigation or close reading: assembling evidence across all activity categories under transfer
focus: assembling evidence across all activity categories
essentialQuestion: What can I now do, and what am I choosing to carry forward?
materials: the year’s course notebook or digital equivalent
privacySafeScenario: Assemble and present the portfolio to one trusted adult: category evidence, a training principle explained, the revised safety plan, and a justified plan for Grade 10.
studentTask: Learner works assembling evidence across all activity categories assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of assembling evidence across all activity categories degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds assembling evidence across all activity categories assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, video, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of assembling evidence across all activity categories yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, video, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where assembling evidence across all activity categories shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
